note: Our own competency questions, worded so a fresher can answer from college projects, internships or hackathons. Selection drops job-assuming questions for interns and freshers, so none are needed here.

questions.title: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a teammate on a technical approach. How did you resolve it?
Describe a group project where one member was not contributing. What did you do?
Tell me about a time you had to work with someone you found difficult.
Describe a time you changed your mind after hearing a teammate's argument.
Tell me about a time two people on your team were in conflict and you helped them move forward.
Describe a time you had to give a peer feedback on their code or work.
Tell me about a time you received criticism from a teammate. How did you respond?
Describe a time your team missed a deadline. What was your role and what did you change?
Tell me about a time you had to collaborate with people from a different team or discipline.
Describe a time you helped a teammate who was stuck, even though it delayed your own work.
Tell me about a time you had to explain a technical idea to someone without a technical background.
Describe a time you and a reviewer disagreed in a code review.
Tell me about a time you had to work in a team where everyone was remote or in different places.
Describe how you divided work in your last group or team project, and what you would do differently.
Tell me about a time you had to say no to a request from a teammate or senior.
Describe a time you built trust with a new team quickly.
Tell me about a time you had to compromise on your preferred solution for the team.
Describe a time a misunderstanding caused a problem in a team. How was it fixed?
Tell me about a time you mentored or taught a classmate or junior colleague.
Describe a time you had to rely on someone else to finish your part of the work.
Tell me about a time you failed at something important. What did you learn?
Describe a bug you shipped or a mistake in a project. How did you find and fix it?
Tell me about a project that did not go as planned. What would you do differently?
Describe a time you underestimated how long something would take.
Tell me about a time you had to learn a new technology quickly to finish a task.
Describe the hardest technical problem you have debugged.
Tell me about a time you got negative feedback. What did you change afterwards?
Describe a time you made a wrong assumption about requirements.
Tell me about a time you did not meet a goal you set for yourself.
Describe a time a test, exam or interview went badly and how you prepared differently next time.
Tell me about a time you had to recover a project after a setback.
Describe a decision you regret and what it taught you.
Tell me about a time you had to admit you did not know something.
Describe a time you broke something in production or in a shared environment.
Tell me about a time you persisted with a problem for a long time before solving it.
Describe something you taught yourself outside of class or work, and how you went about it.
Tell me about a time you had to abandon an approach halfway through.
Describe a time you had too many things to do and something slipped.
Tell me about a skill you were weak at and how you improved it.
Describe a time you asked for help later than you should have.
Tell me about a time you took ownership of a problem nobody else was handling.
Describe a project you led from idea to finish.
Tell me about a time you went beyond what was asked of you.
Describe a time you had to make a decision with incomplete information.
Tell me about a time you convinced others to adopt your idea.
Describe a time you improved a process, tool or workflow for your team.
Tell me about a time you had to prioritise between several urgent tasks.
Describe a time you organised an event, club activity or hackathon team.
Tell me about a time you set a high standard for your work when it would have been easier not to.
Describe a time you noticed a risk early and acted on it.
Tell me about a time you had to deliver under a tight deadline.
Describe a time you simplified something complicated.
Tell me about a time you took a calculated risk.
Describe a time you had to influence someone senior to you.
Tell me about a time you owned a mistake made by your team.
Describe the project you are proudest of and your specific contribution.
Tell me about a time you used data to make a decision.
Describe a time you had to keep a project moving when people lost interest.
Tell me about a time you took initiative to learn what users actually needed.
Describe a time you balanced quality against speed and how you chose.
What is a strength that makes you a good engineer? Give an example of it in action.
What is a weakness you are working on, and what are you doing about it?
What feedback do you hear most often from teammates or teachers?
Which part of software engineering do you enjoy most, and which least?
How would a close teammate describe how you work?
What is something you do better than most of your peers?
What kind of work environment helps you do your best work?
How do you handle pressure and tight deadlines?
What is one thing you would like to get much better at in the next year?
How do you keep your technical skills up to date?
How do you approach a problem you have never seen before?
Which of your skills is most underrated by others?
Why do you want to work as a software engineer?
What are you looking for in your next role?
Where do you see yourself in three to five years?
What kind of problems excite you the most?
Why are you interested in this company?
What would make you a good fit for this team?
Which technology or product do you admire, and why?
What motivates you to do your best work?
